messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler 'gpu-pool-eu' reached max_node_count. Throttling observed. Queue growth 600% in last 5m. Severity: high. Pager sent to #incidents.
Alice (oncall): seeing elevated 429s and request queues backing up. Confirming region: eu-west-1.
Samir: logs show HPA/cluster-autoscaler refusing scale: 'max nodes reached for nodegroup gpu-pool-eu'. Also K8s pending pods due to Unschedulable.
Maria: customers reporting slow responses on embeddings endpoints and higher latencies for streaming. Any impacted accounts we can call out?
Claire (customer-success): three customers reported errors via support: ACME, Fitlytics, and TutorAI. ACME reports 50% of requests failing with 429. They're asking for ETA.
Alice (oncall): ack. Quick mitigation plan: 1) try temporary fallback to smaller model variant for non-critical traffic 2) enable burst capacity if infra can bump node limit 3) throttling policy adjust for bursty clients. I'll start with model fallback.
Samir: prepared a canary switch. Patch to routing config:
```yaml
- route: /v1/generate
  preferred_model: redwood-medium-v1
  fallback_model: redwood-small-quant
  traffic_split: 85/15
```
I'll roll to 10% first.
Ben (ops-lead): we should request a manual nodegroup max increase from infra for the duration. Samir, estimate time to provision additional GPUs?
Samir: from previous tests ~6-9 minutes to scale up new instances if infra approves and quota is available. If quota hits, may be longer.
Alice (oncall): infra request going out. @infra-bot can you open a manual-cap bump? include justification: production outage, eu-west-1, nodepool gpu-pool-eu, requested +8 nodes, duration 1h.
infra-bot: Manual cap bump request submitted to infra-runbook queue. Ticket #IR-7284. Required approvals: infra-owner and capacity-team. ETA to approve: ~10-15m.
Maria: meanwhile, can we reduce batch sizes to lower per-request GPU utilization? Patch will be low-risk.
Samir: pushing runtime config change to reduce default batch_size from 64 -> 32 for affected model routes. Rolling now.
Alice (oncall): kubectl snapshot while this is happening:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep "Pending|CrashLoopBackOff|Running"
inference-gen-0   Pending   0/1   0     0s
inference-gen-1   Running   1/1   0     5m
inference-emb-2   Pending   0/1   0     20s
```
Also cluster-autoscaler logs show:
```
I0412 14:30:02 scale_up.go:234] NodeGroup gpu-pool-eu can't scale: reached max nodes (16)
I0412 14:30:07 scale_up.go:245] Not scaling further
```
Claire (customer-success): ACME is asking for an ETA. Please provide an interim message: "We're actively mitigating a capacity issue in eu-west-1; temporary degradations possible. Our engineers are on it; we'll update in 15m."
Ben (ops-lead): agreed. Alice, send the customer note. I'll follow infra approval path and coordinate slips.
Alice (oncall): note posted to ACME and internal status page. Updating channel.
infra-bot: Capacity-team approved. Infra-owner approved. Executing nodegroup update: gpu-pool-eu max_nodes 16 -> 24. Provisioning started.
Samir: seeing new provisioning events in cloud console. Instances spawning.
Alice (oncall): monitoring queue length. Current queued requests: 18k -> starting to drop?
Samir: new nodes became Ready at +7m. K8s scheduler bound several pending pods. Post-scale kubectl snapshot:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=gpu-pool-eu
NAME             STATUS   ROLES    AGE
gpu-node-17      Ready    <none>   30s
... (total 24 nodes)
```
Pods transitioning to Running.
Maria: reducing backoff and restoring routing after observing success metrics. Rolling traffic back to primary model.
Alice (oncall): latency and 429s decreasing. Support reports ACME seeing success rate improving to 95%.
Claire (customer-success): ACME confirmed degraded behavior is resolved for now and appreciates fast response. They asked for root cause and follow-up.
Ben (ops-lead): Next steps: 1) postmortem to include autoscaler config (max_nodes rationale), prediction/alerting gaps (queue growth vs autoscaler thresholds), and playbook for manual cap bumps. 2) Evaluate emergency quota reserve for EU. 3) Run load test to validate future scale.
Alice (oncall): I'm taking handoff to SRE for postmortem. Assigning action items and will update the incident ticket #IR-7284. Closing live coordination thread. :white_check_mark:
Samir: archived logs and metrics links added to ticket.
infra-bot: Manual cap will be reverted to 16 at 2026-04-12T16:00:00Z unless extended.
Ben (ops-lead): thanks team. Great coordination.
Alice (oncall): final note: incident duration ~36m from alert to recovery. Root cause: autoscaler max_nodes conservative cap + insufficient prewarming for predictable batch spike. Will draft postmortem.
